transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Laura Chen (Acme Legal), Matt Rivera (Acme Procurement), Imani Okoro (Acme Security), Daniel Park (Acme Engineering)

Summary: quick procurement + legal review of MSA/DPA, discuss SLAs and onboarding process, ask for redlines and run benchmarks.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Jordan from Redwood, i'm here with Priya our SE and Sam from CSM. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Laura Chen: Good, thanks. We wanted to go through the MSA and DPA and make sure timelines are realistic. we have a few redlines around data residency and audit logs.
00:18 Jordan Lee: Totally, that's exactly what we want to cover. Our plan is to run through the high level items — SLAs, encryption/KMS, SSO, and then deployment options and pricing. Priya will cover the technical bits.
00:31 Priya Nair: Hi all, quick note, i'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private, where the audit logs live, and what the onboarding bench— benchmark looks like. sorry for the slight echo, i'm on a weird headset.
00:46 Matt Rivera: On the timeline side, procurement needs a signed MSA and DPA before we can greenlight any paid pilots. Also need approvals from finance for pricing tier.
00:58 Sam Ortiz: Great, we've seen that pattern a lot. we'll try to make the legal redlines process smooth. Jordan, we'll send a pricing sheet and the standard onboarding SOW after this call.
01:10 Daniel Park: From eng, we want to understand network setup for the private deployment. VPC peering? direct connect? also curious about KMS integration and whether we can keep keys in HSM.
01:24 Priya Nair: For private we support VPC peering and on-prem options; we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, or customer HSM via PKCS11). note, sometimes the term 'KV cache' shows up in our docs — that's key-value cache for model state, not encryption keys, just to avoid confusion.
01:42 Imani Okoro: Can you also confirm where audit logs are stored and retention options — we need 7 years for certain workflows.
01:50 Priya Nair: Yes, audit logs can be exported to your SIEM, they can be stored in customer-owned S3 buckets for hosted (if you choose log export), and for private they're local to your environment so retention is in your control. We have an add-on for extended retention.
02:05 Laura Chen: Looking at the DPA, section 4.2 on sub-processing — we need Redwood to confirm subprocessors list and commit to 30 days notice prior to adding a new subprocessor.
02:17 Jordan Lee: We can commit to providing a subprocessor list and 30 days' notice — i'll confirm with legal and get that in writing.
02:25 Matt Rivera: Pricing – we need a clear table of unit costs and committed monthly minimums for dedicated. Also what happens if we exceed committed capacity temporarily?
02:36 Jordan Lee: For dedicated we offer commit tiers with burst options. overage pricing is X per token for burst; we'll send the exact table. for hosted, it's pay as you go with volume discounts.
02:49 Priya Nair: To be explicit about latency SLOs — hosted low-latency SLO is 99th percentile under Y ms for common models, dedicated has stricter SLAs with reserved GPUs. for private, SLOs depend on customer infra but we provide a recommended ops runbook.
03:06 Daniel Park: Are there any model fallbacks for high load? we don't want live failures during peak times.
03:14 Priya Nair: Yes, we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants across tiers/regions. if dedicated capacity is saturated, requests can route to a cost tier or a less-costly variant depending on your policy.
03:28 Imani Okoro: On encryption in transit and at rest, do you support customer-managed keys exclusively? we need to avoid Redwood possessing plaintext data long term.
03:38 Jordan Lee: We support customer-managed keys for at rest. for hosted, data is encrypted at rest and in transit, and you can opt into CMK so Redwood doesn't have the master key. For Private, keys never leave your control.
03:50 Laura Chen: Ok on MSA redlines — we have three asks: explicit data residency clause, subprocessor notice 30 days, and indemnity cap adjustments. is Redwood open to negotiating those?
04:02 Jordan Lee: We're open to discussing. indemnity caps are often a legal negotiation — we'll flag that to our legal team but typically we try to be balanced. i'll push on priority of these asks and get back with suggestions.
04:15 Matt Rivera: Also need to understand onboarding timeline — if we sign by end of April, when can we go live with a small pilot?
04:24 Sam Ortiz: Our standard timeline for a pilot is 2–3 weeks after contract signature for hosted, 4–6 weeks for dedicated setup, and private can vary (6–10 weeks) depending on network approvals.
04:37 Daniel Park: For the perf benchmark, what configs do you recommend we run?
04:42 Priya Nair: We'll run three configs: hosted (baseline model A), dedicated (pin same model on reserved GPUs), and private (if desired). we'll measure latency at 2k and 8k token contexts, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
04:59 Laura Chen: Who is the legal contact on Redwood side? for redlines who should we send them to?
05:04 Jordan Lee: Send redlines to contracts@redwood.com and i'll loop in our legal ops — and i'll personally follow up.

05:15 [15:10] - small silence while people review the MSA PDF everyone was shared
05:25 Matt Rivera: Regarding the DPA, we need clarity on data deletion timelines post-contract and proof of deletion.
05:33 Priya Nair: We can provide deletion certificates and runbook details — in hosted we delete logs after retention period unless retention export is enabled. we'll include deletion certificate language in the DPA redline.
05:48 Laura Chen: On SLAs, we need an availability SLA at 99.9% for production endpoints with credits for outages. can you commit to that for dedicated?
06:00 Jordan Lee: For dedicated we can discuss 99.9% SLA with contractual credits — exact numbers depend on scale but we can propose language in the SLA addendum.
06:12 Imani Okoro: For compliance, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? our auditors will ask for the reports.
06:20 Jordan Lee: Yes, we maintain SOC 2 Type II and are ISO certified — i'll share the attestation and a short summary.
06:27 Laura Chen: Great, please send them.

06:35 [06:35] Priya Nair: Quick technical clarification — when you say private, do you want the control plane in our VPC, or fully air-gapped on-prem?
06:44 Daniel Park: We prefer control plane in our VPC with data plane on-prem for sensitive workloads. can you support that hybrid?
06:52 Priya Nair: We support a hybrid deployment. control plane can be customer-managed in a VPC and the compute can be in your on-prem clusters; we have connectors for that. we'll include architecture diagrams in the runbook.
07:06 Matt Rivera: On procurement cadence — we need finance sign-off for recurring commit. is there a minimum term for dedicated?
07:15 Jordan Lee: Typical terms are 12 months for committed dedicated, but we can discuss 6-month pilot terms with limited commit depending on volume. we'll include options in pricing sheet.
07:26 Laura Chen: A couple of DPA specifics: data subject requests, breach notification timelines (we need 72 hours), and subprocessor obligations.
07:35 Jordan Lee: 72-hour breach notification is reasonable for many customers — we'll confirm with legal, but we should be able to align.
07:43 Imani Okoro: Regarding SSO: we use Okta, want SCIM provisioning and SAML 2.0. does Redwood support SCIM?
07:51 Priya Nair: Yes, SCIM for user provisioning and SAML 2.0 are supported. we have docs in the SSO playbook i'll send.
08:02 Daniel Park: For audit trail access, do you provide role-based access controls so only certain teams can see logs?
08:08 Priya Nair: Yes RBAC is supported in Redwood Console. you can map groups from SSO to roles. for private, it's delegated to your IAM but we provide integration guidance.
08:20 [08:20] Laura Chen: ok, switching back to pricing approvals — can you email a final price sheet with committed vs burst pricing and the terms for overage? procurement needs that to prepare the PO.
08:31 Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we'll attach a clear matrix with committed tiers, burst rates, and any discounts for annual prepay.
08:38 Matt Rivera: Also need a cost model for 10M tokens/month and 100M tokens/month so finance can compare.
08:46 Sam Ortiz: We'll run a cost model for those two volume points and include both hosted and dedicated estimates.
08:52 Laura Chen: Regarding vendor onboarding, what's the typical checklist? security review, pen test, SLA sign-off?
08:59 Sam Ortiz: Our onboarding checklist: 1) legal sign-off (MSA/DPA), 2) security questionnaire and attestations, 3) SSO/KMS integration, 4) pilot configuration and benchmark, 5) go-live checklist and runbooks. we'll share the checklist doc.
09:12 Matt Rivera: Will Redwood require us to sign a separate DPA or is it embedded in the MSA?
09:19 Jordan Lee: We can do either — our standard is a separate DPA that gets attached to the MSA. if you prefer clauses inside the MSA we can fold them in.
09:28 Laura Chen: We typically prefer a separate DPA. please send your standard DPA and we'll redline.
09:33 Jordan Lee: Noted. Jordan will send both the MSA and DPA and a redlineable copy.

09:45 [09:45] Priya Nair: A quick note on private performance: quantization and kernel selection matter a lot for 8k contexts. we can provide a recommended quantization profile to balance cost and accuracy. sometimes docs call it "quant" or 'quantiz' and that's why we have the recommendation sheet.
10:02 Daniel Park: Perf numbers are important for finance to sign off. can you commit to real numbers from your internal tests?
10:09 Priya Nair: We'll run the benchmark in our staging environment with a reproducible harness and share raw logs and summary. we aim to be transparent.
10:18 Laura Chen: On indemnity, our lawyers want a reciprocal indemnity for IP claims and a cap at 1x ARR. how flexible is Redwood on that?
10:27 Jordan Lee: Indemnity language is always a negotiation. we'll surface that to legal ops — i can't promise but we'll try to find middle ground.
10:35 Matt Rivera: Any concerns about our regulatory posture? Acme handles some healthcare data — do you have BAAs?
10:43 Jordan Lee: We can support HIPAA workloads; we have a BAA we can share. for more regulated workloads, private deployment is recommended.
10:52 Imani Okoro: Do you do penetration tests and share the summary?
10:56 Jordan Lee: Yes, we run annual pen tests and will share the summary report under NDA.
11:04 Laura Chen: Ok that's helpful. for the DPA can Redwood accept data residency language restricting EU data to EU-based regions for some workloads?
11:13 Jordan Lee: Yes, region pinning is supported via routing policies; we can explicitly write that into the DPA.
11:21 Matt Rivera: One final procurement ask — will Redwood accept electronic signatures and a PO for payment?
11:29 Jordan Lee: Yes we accept e-signatures (DocuSign) and POs; invoice terms can be net 30 or negotiable for enterprise.
11:36 [11:36] - brief crosstalk about calendar scheduling
11:45 Jordan Lee: To recap: we'll send redlineable MSA & DPA, pricing matrix + cost models, SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/KMS playbook, onboarding checklist, and runbook/arch diagrams. Priya will run perf benchmarks and share logs. Laura to send Acme redlines. we'll aim to get redlines and responses within the next week.
11:58 Laura Chen: That works. i'll circulate internally and aim to get redlines by Friday.
12:05 Matt Rivera: We'll also review the pricing and get procurement approvals.
12:12 Jordan Lee: Great — we'll you know follow up with the bundle of docs by end of day tomorrow.

12:20 Closing notes: People thanked each other and agreed next meeting would be legal redlines call if needed on 2026-04-12.
12:28 End of recording.
